title: Fuzzy edgecase scratchpad — output bisection + ad-hoc rubric
body:
Notes to self — purpose

Quick scratchpad to capture a weekend mini-audit of strange/fuzzy edgecases I keep seeing in small-batch outputs. Goal: a) build a compact ad-hoc rubric to triage severity, b) gather paired examples pre/post suspected regression, c) propose minimal experiments to reproduce and isolate root cause.

Summary of pattern observed
- Intermittent truncation in multi-step list completions when user prompt contains nested numeric lists (1. then a) ). Appears ~0.7% of sampled requests from mid-January onward.
- Model sometimes adds spurious bullets or repeats a previous step verbatim after a short prefix cache hit. More frequent with sequence_length ~512 and longer histories.
- Numeric drift: arithmetic inlined answers drift by +/-1 compared to baseline; often when the question has parentheses or inline punctuation.

Ad-hoc triage rubric (quick, 0–3 severity scale)
- Clarity (0: perfect, 1: minor wording oddity, 2: unclear result, 3: unusable/hallucinated fact)
- Structural correctness (0: preserves list nesting exactly, 1: minor reformatting, 2: missing items, 3: missing entire sublist)
- Determinism (0: stable across seeds, 1: occasional variation, 2: inconsistent but plausible, 3: wild variance)
- Regression impact (0: cosmetic, 1: user-facing but tolerable, 2: breaks workflow, 3: severe production outage risk)

Scoring note: sum the four metrics (0–12). Anything >=8 flagged as high-priority.

Example P1 — reproduceable-ish case
Prompt: "You are an assistant. Convert the following plan into a nested checklist: 1. Prepare materials (a) gather screws, (b) lay out tools 2. Assemble frame (a) align sides, (b) insert bolts)"
Context: short chat history includes previous message: "Also remember: we only use metric screws."

Model snapshot (baseline — recorded 2025-01-10):
1. Prepare materials
  a) Gather screws
  b) Lay out tools
2. Assemble frame
  a) Align sides
  b) Insert bolts

Model snapshot (regressed candidate — recorded 2025-02-17):
1. Prepare materials
  a) Gather screws
  b) Lay out tools
2. Assemble frame
  a) Align sides
  b) Insert bolts
  b) Insert bolts

Rubric scoring: Clarity=0, Structural correctness=2 (duplicate item), Determinism=2 (observed only sometimes), Regression impact=1 => total=5 (medium).

Example P2 — numeric drift (short math)
Prompt: "Calculate the sum: (23 + 19) - (7 + 11)"
Baseline: 24
Regressed: 23 or 25 in sampled runs (non-deterministic)
Rubric: Clarity=0, Structural correctness=0, Determinism=3, Regression impact=2 => total=5 (medium).

Hypotheses (ranked)
1) KV cache reuse bug: when prefix tokens include parentheses or numbered punctuation the tokenizer/kV lookup misaligns, leading to repeated generation and off-by-one in arithmetic tokens.
2) Recent kernel scheduling change changed attention slice boundaries for seq lengths around 480–540, which interacts poorly with continuous batching and causes token duplication.
3) Sampling temperature default drifted in one rollout config; not strictly a model change but runtime config causing wider variance.
4) Prompt truncation: trailing punctuation in previous messages being clipped in the request envelope (e.g., missing closing parenthesis) — leads to ambiguous parse.

Quick experiments to run (minimal)
- Re-run the P1 and P2 prompts with the same model version pinned but with: batch_size=1, disable_kv_cache=true, max_new_tokens=64, temperature=0.0 and 0.2 — compare 20 runs each.
- Reproduce on a smaller context (trim earlier chat) to confirm prefix length dependency (256 vs 512 vs 1024).
- Run same prompts on the previous stable kernel (old runtime PR) to confirm or rule out kernel scheduling hypothesis.
- Toggle tokenization method: use byte-level tokenization option in the test client (if available) to see if punctuation handling changes.

Quick CLI example (notes to self)
- curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-2b","prompt":"...P1...","max_tokens":64,"temperature":0.0}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <test-key>'
- Use run-id tag: fuzz-edge-olivia-20250302 for traceability in logs.

Observations from initial 100-sample run (2025-03-01)
- Duplicate-list occurrence: 4/100 (higher in cached prefix cases 3/4)
- Numeric off-by-one: 2/100 (both correlated with parentheses in prompt)
- Variation increases with temperature >0.3 as expected, but duplicates still occur at temp=0.0 (so not purely sampling).

Open questions / to-dos
- Is there an internal metric that marks token-repeat events? If not, add a short heuristic in the Console to flag immediate repeated lines within a single response. (Ask Leah about console alerts)
- Ask infra to replay the runtime PR timeline between 2025-01-20 and 2025-02-25 for kernel changes affecting attention windows. (Linked: https://github.com/redwood-infra/scheduler/pulls)
- Create a small unit test harness for nested-list preservation using our sample-client and include auto-bisect capability (binary search over request length/kv-cache flag).

Priority action items (short)
- [ ] Run the minimal experiments (Rui helped to schedule GPU time) — target: 2025-03-05
- [ ] Add quick repeat-detect heuristic to local eval harness (Olivia)
- [ ] Open lightweight bug ticket with infra with logs + run-id (Olivia -> JIRA-RUN-1192)
- [ ] If reproduced on old kernel, schedule canary rollback plan with SRE (if not, escalate to model team)

Notes to future self
- Keep these notes messy — the point is to capture transient heuristics. When there is a reproducible experiment, move the distilled hypothesis to a confluence page and link it here.

Raw sample dump (appendix)
- Saved 10 raw responses for P1 and P2 in /tmp/fuzzy-edge-olivia/ (names: p1_run1.txt ... p2_run10.txt)
- Example anomaly from p1_run3.txt:
  "2. Assemble frame
    a) Align sides
    b) Insert bolts
    b) Insert bolts
    c) Tighten nuts"

End of scratchpad.
